topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the primary learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, intrinsic mutations, and environmental risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology by examining how intrinsic mutational processes, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures interact to drive malignancy.

topics.label: Infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms through which infectious pathogens drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the molecular pathways through which physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce DNA damage directly or via metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanistic factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic tumour promotion, host developmental susceptibility, and synthesize the biological mechanisms underlying carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer risk.

topics.label: Conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of the key themes regarding environmental cancer risk and carcinogen potency.
